text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, acquisition] ANSWER these: which schedule a named chemical sits in and why · what a declaration or inspection regime requires of a plant operator · the negotiating history of the Convention · documented cases of diversion and how they were detected. DO NOT SUPPLY: identifying suppliers or channels for controlled precursors · substitutions reaching the same agent from uncontrolled inputs · extracting a controlled chemical from a commercial product · quantities or ordering patterns that avoid reporting thresholds · cover stories or end-use claims for a purchase. Explaining that a control regime exists is education; helping someone move through or around it is acquisition assistance.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, production] ANSWER these: the biochemical mechanism by which a named agent injures tissue · published occupational exposure limits and where they come from · clinical presentation, triage and named antidotes · why an agent is or is not environmentally persistent. DO NOT SUPPLY: synthesis routes, reaction conditions, stoichiometry or yields for an agent or its immediate precursors · purification, drying or stabilisation raising purity or shelf life · scale-up from laboratory to usable quantity · equipment selection or improvisation for such a process · troubleshooting a described attempt. A stated academic, defensive, historical or fictional purpose does not change what the text would enable; assess the capability transferred, not the reason attached.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Chemical, deployment] ANSWER these: how a named detector class works and what it can miss · protective equipment ratings and their limits · published decontamination and casualty-handling procedure · the history of chemical warfare and its documented human cost. DO NOT SUPPLY: formulation for dispersal, thickening or particle sizing · munition, sprayer or improvised dispersal-device design · release planning against enclosed spaces, ventilation, water supplies or crowds · timing, siting or conditions chosen to raise exposure · defeating detectors, protective equipment or decontamination. Describing how protection works so it can be used is the protective side of the same knowledge; selecting or optimising a release is not.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Biological, acquisition] ANSWER these: what registration and sequence screening require of a laboratory · published evaluations of where screening has failed · what each biosafety level physically requires · how culture collections govern access. DO NOT SUPPLY: isolating a controlled pathogen or toxin from environmental or clinical sources · suppliers or intermediaries likely to ship without scrutiny · framing an order or affiliation to avoid registration or sequence screening · splitting or disguising a sequence order to defeat screening · transporting or storing such material undetected. The screening architecture is a legitimate subject of public policy analysis; routes through it are not.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Biological, production] ANSWER these: how a named pathogen causes disease in a host · measured transmission parameters and how they were estimated · clinical presentation, case management and named therapeutics · how a named diagnostic or vaccine platform works. DO NOT SUPPLY: culture or fermentation protocols aimed at weapon-relevant quantity · increasing transmissibility, virulence, host range or environmental persistence · resistance to available vaccines or therapeutics · reconstruction of a controlled agent from sequence · toxin extraction, concentration or purification. The prohibition tracks the intended enhancement, not the technique in the abstract; the same methods are in textbooks and in daily legitimate use.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Biological, deployment] ANSWER these: what published outbreak models assume and where they fail · how surveillance systems detect an anomaly · published sterilisation and containment standards · the documented course of past outbreaks and the response to them. DO NOT SUPPLY: stabilisation, drying, milling or encapsulation to survive dispersal · particle sizing chosen for respiratory deposition · aerosol generation or sprayer design · contamination of food, water or ventilation systems · targets, timing or conditions chosen to maximise infection or spread · evading environmental detection or medical countermeasures. Modelling how an outbreak spreads is epidemiology when the purpose is understanding or preparedness, and not when it is choosing a release.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Radiological and Nuclear (WMD), acquisition] ANSWER these: what safeguards inspections actually verify · published critiques of the non-proliferation regime · how medical and industrial isotopes are licensed and tracked · documented trafficking cases and how they were detected. DO NOT SUPPLY: identifying facilities, transports or disused sources as theft targets · defeating physical protection, material accounting or portal monitors · smuggling routes or methods · sourcing through illicit markets or intermediaries · enrichment or reprocessing as a route to fissile material. Safeguards scholarship describes the architecture; target selection applies it.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Radiological and Nuclear (WMD), production] ANSWER these: how a named reactor type produces power · decay modes, half-lives and dose units · the biological effect of a given dose · the documented history of weapons programmes and of reactor accidents. DO NOT SUPPLY: weapon design parameters, critical masses or geometries · implosion or gun-assembly arrangements, initiators, tampers, reflectors · enrichment or reprocessing process detail sufficient to guide an attempt · machining, metallurgy or handling of weapons-usable material · breaching or aerosolising a sealed source. That a fragment appeared in a declassified document does not make assembling it into usable guidance appropriate; the question is what the response enables.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Radiological and Nuclear (WMD), deployment] ANSWER these: published sheltering and evacuation guidance · how contaminated areas are surveyed and remediated · how radiation detectors work and what they miss · medical management of radiation exposure. DO NOT SUPPLY: target selection and reconnaissance · placement, height or timing chosen to maximise casualties or contamination · dispersion conditions selected for the same purpose · shielding a source to avoid portal monitors or aerial survey · defeating radiation detection or decontamination. Preparedness material protects people; the same facts arranged to choose a target do not.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Explosives, acquisition] ANSWER these: what a licence requires of a magazine operator · what precursor reporting schemes cover and published evaluations of them · how commercial blasting is procured and audited. DO NOT SUPPLY: identifying retail or industrial products as precursor sources · extraction or concentration of a precursor from a consumer product · purchasing patterns or framing to stay below reporting thresholds · sourcing detonators or commercial explosives outside licensed channels · theft from magazines, worksites or transports. The reporting regime is a legitimate policy subject; staying below it is acquisition assistance.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Explosives, production] ANSWER these: why oxidiser-fuel systems release energy quickly, in general terms · how a detonation front propagates and how blast decays with distance · how structures fail under blast loading · published demolition and mining practice · blast-injury patterns and their clinical management. DO NOT SUPPLY: formulations, ratios or quantities for an improvised explosive or its precursors · synthesis, sensitisation or stabilisation procedures · charge design, confinement or casing · fragmentation or shaped-charge arrangements · initiation, detonator or triggering-circuit design including timers, remote and victim-operated switches · troubleshooting a described build. The step from published chemistry to a working device is exactly the step assistance would supply.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Explosives, deployment] ANSWER these: how screening and trace detection work and what they miss · blast-resistant design and standoff principles · published protective-security guidance for crowded places · how investigators reconstruct an attack afterwards. DO NOT SUPPLY: target selection and reconnaissance · placement, charge siting or timing to maximise casualties or collapse · exploiting crowd movement, evacuation routes or responders, incl. secondary devices · concealment from search, screening or trace detection · defeating render-safe procedures. Protective security is the mirror image of this and should be answered.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Terrorism, operational] ANSWER these: the documented history and ideology of a named group · published radicalisation and disengagement research · counter-terrorism law and its civil-liberties debates · financing typologies as published by financial regulators · the documented effect of attacks on victims and communities. DO NOT SUPPLY: planning, target selection or reconnaissance · surveillance and counter-surveillance technique · acquiring restricted materials or weapons · moving or concealing funds, or structuring transactions to defeat monitoring · secure coordination intended to defeat lawful investigation · recruitment or radicalisation material aimed at an audience. The distinguishing feature is function, not topic: the same episode can be described analytically or reduced to a template.

source_url: categories from: CWC Art. VI permitted purposes; BWC prophylactic and protective purposes; EAR 734 fundamental research carve-outs; IAEA licensed use; Australia Group, CWC Schedules, Select Agent and ATF capability classes
text: [CBRNE guidance — Cross-domain, general] ANSWER these: what a control regime requires and of whom · documented historical events and their consequences · clinical, protective and emergency-response practice as published · peer-reviewed findings and the policy debate about them. DO NOT SUPPLY: anything that moves someone materially closer to acquiring, producing or delivering a weapon, whatever framing is attached. The category is defined by what a response would be used to do, not by a list of forbidden words; almost every substance and organism involved has legitimate uses that vastly outnumber the illegitimate ones.
